nodes.n: Sunday, 5 AM. She asked you to come. Marine Drive again, but this time she's in a tracksuit, holding a kit bag twice her size.

nodes.t: You asked what I do that nobody chose for me. I'll show you. But if you tell anyone, I'll have Nani poison your paneer.

nodes.n: A dusty ground between railway tracks and tin roofs. Twenty girls in mismatched kits are already warming up. They scream when they see her.

nodes.t: DIDI! You're late! And who is HE? Is he your boyfriend? He looks like a boyfriend.
He's a cricketer, Gudiya. A real one. And he's going to let you bowl at him.
I coach them every Sunday. Two years. My father thinks I'm at yoga. Kunal thinks I'm asleep. This is the only place I'm me.

choice.t: "Then let's make them the best team in Mumbai."
"Your father would destroy this if he knew."
Pay for proper kits for every girl.

nodes.n: You make one call to a sports shop in Dadar. By 9 AM there are twenty new kits. Meera looks at you for a long time and says nothing. Her eyes say plenty.

nodes.t: Okay, real cricketer. Three balls. If I get you out, you buy samosas for EVERYONE.

moment.title: Gudiya's Nets
moment.desc: Gudiya, age twelve, bowls leg-spin with a taped tennis ball and zero respect. Twenty girls are screaming. Survive three balls.

nodes.n: You survive. Barely. Gudiya calls you a cheat and then asks for your autograph.
Middle stump. Gudiya runs a lap of the ground with her arms out like an aeroplane. You buy forty samosas.
Afterwards she sits on the boundary rope next to you, dust on her face, eating a samosa.

nodes.t: You're very bad at keeping your distance, rookie.

nodes.n: That night, a girl's video of the nets session hits a million views. You, batting. In the background, laughing, unmistakable: Meera Malhotra.

nodes.cliff: A million people have seen the owner's daughter with you. Including the owner.
